message: SPEC required a tracked, append-per-tool-call provenance log plus per-commit [stage:][task:] tags. Foundry's clean-tree check on task_done and its fixed `<ID>:` subjects and MCP-authored progress/review commits forced workarounds: a gitignored live log with phase-end snapshots, and a commit-msg hook. The skill has no guidance for projects that must log or tag Foundry's own activity.

Canterbury corpus URL (https://corpus.canterbury.ac.nz/resources/cantrbry.tar.gz, the only allowlisted URL per SPEC/guard) returns HTTP 403 from Cloudflare bot management in this sandbox network, confirmed with retries and full browser-like headers; not a script bug. Silesia (also allowlisted) downloads fine (200). Per PLAN.md P0-08 explicit instruction ("Canterbury is required: if it cannot be downloaded after 3 attempts, block the task"), this blocks P0-08 and cascades to skip most corpus-dependent downstream tasks, which is a large portion of the remaining plan. This is an environment/network constraint outside the implementer's control, not something a different script approach can fix.

Coordinator relayed operator instructions to unblock P0-08 (a human downloaded the Canterbury corpus and gave me the verified file+sha256). I implemented the actual fix (fetch-corpora.sh --from-file, SOURCES.json, README.md, committed as 361e93c) and it fully resolves the blocker on disk. But there is no MCP tool to reopen a [!] blocked (or [-] skipped) task: foundry_task_done requires the task to be 'in progress' (foundry_task_next must select it first), and foundry_task_next only ever selects the first [~] or first [ ] task, never reconsidering [!]/[-] rows. My instructions also explicitly forbid hand-editing docs/PROGRESS.md. Net effect: P0-08 stays marked blocked and its dependents (P0-09, P0-10, P0-11, P1-03, P1-11, P1-12) stay skipped in PROGRESS.md even though the underlying data now exists and the work is committed, and I have no sanctioned way to flip that state within this run. A `foundry_task_reopen` (or similar) tool would let a resolved-blocker mid-run actually get picked back up.

foundry_mutate has no per-run wall-clock timeout short of the command's timeoutMs (1800s): a mutation that makes a test spin forever (e.g. an infinite decode loop) stalled the reviewer for 30 minutes and left orphaned spinning test binaries that had to be killed by hand. Parallel foundry_mutate calls also appear to queue behind a hung one and time out too.

foundry_review_submit's unblock reset P0-08 to todo but left the 17 tasks cascade-skipped behind it as [-] skipped (counts: skipped 17 after submit). The reviewer has no sanctioned way to re-open skipped dependents, so the corpus-dependent acceptance/conformance tasks will not run in the fix round unless a human or controller re-opens them.

foundry_mutate has no per-call timeout override, so a mutation suspected of hanging `make test` (R1-02's own would-have-caught mutation) would burn the full 30-minute verify timeout; I had to reproduce it in a scratchpad copy of the crate with `timeout 60` instead.

git commit -m with a HEREDOC body that merely mentioned "curl" in prose (describing a fix to URL-extraction from Bash curl calls) was denied by the cleanroom guard's post-lockdown curl-denial pattern, even though the command was `git commit`, not `curl`. The guard's Bash pattern-matches the word "curl" anywhere in the command string, including inside a quoted commit message. Had to reword the commit message to avoid the literal word.
